review.brief_reason: The repeated denominator would factor as (x2 - 26.17108295984481) times the cosine sum only if 155.6172914296232 exactly equaled 26.17108295984481*5.946154068916144. The decimal constants leave a nonzero residual. Although tiny, it causes arbitrarily large value differences near x2=26.17108295984481 on the common domain. The domains also differ at and near the resulting singular sets.
review.counterexample: Take x2=26.17108295984482, x3=x5=1.5707963267948966, x1=7.7303225354777406, and x4=1.4364693687245928. Both expressions are real and defined, but the nonzero constant-product residual is comparable to or larger than (x2-26.17108295984481) times the cosine sum, producing a large value mismatch.
